text:
alex: Quick heads-up: hitting weird SSE framing on Node SDK during a streaming sample app. Duplicate chunks + final 'data: [DONE]' arriving before last chunk.

maria: ugh can you paste logs? sample app or real prod?

alex: sample app, node sdk 0.9.2, local proxy -> hosted. Steps: start stream, immediately cancel client, sometimes server still sends one extra chunk and we see ordering like: chunk N, [DONE], chunk N+1.

sam: we saw similar with the python sdk a while back; was fixed by buffering on client. node sdk uses eventsource parser that emits on newline only.

alex: logs:
```
stream recv: {"id":1, "delta":"foo"}
stream recv: {"id":1, "delta":"bar"}
stream recv: data: [DONE]
stream recv: {"id":1, "delta":"baz"}
```

jia: is the client disconnect timing causing proxy to flush partial buffer? which proxy? nginx or dev-proxy?

alex: dev-proxy (local). We saw it too when using cloudflare workers in front. Seems like chunk coalescing + timeout flush.

maria: Re auth/retry, could be our retry middleware triggering a partial re-request? But for streaming we avoid retries.

sam: Node SDK parity note: Python SDK uses a small delay to wait for stream end, Node didn't. Maybe we should add a configurable finalization window.

jia: Is there a reproducer repo? could add to sample-apps so onboarding sees it.

alex: yes i'll push repro. For now workaround is to wait for data: [DONE] before closing connection and ignore messages after done.

ci-bot: CI pipeline for sample-apps/streaming-repro triggered by alex

maria: We should also log last-event-id and buffer chunk boundaries. Maybe make server send an explicit final event with seq number.

sam: Agree. Also check auth middleware: when token refresh happens mid-stream we should not re-initiate request.

alex: Filed GH: sample-apps#89 with repro and logs. Tagging devex for parity fix.

jia: I'll add a note in onboarding doc about expected streaming behavior and the node/parity issue.

maria: Can someone pick up a small SDK PR? Node: add 50ms finalize buffer on stream end + ignore events after [DONE]; Python keep as-is but doc note.

sam: I'll do the Node PR tomorrow. Reference: convo + sample-apps#89

alex: thanks! this has bitten a couple of folks during hacks. will update thread when PR merged.

maria: :thumbsup:
